title: Page before expensive aggregation on large list screens
summary: On large list screens, filter and page candidate IDs before running expensive detail joins, window counts, or aggregates; make has-more and approximate totals explicit product contracts.
ai_value: Helps agents avoid turning read-only list views into production load by aggregating the whole result set before bounding the page.

contexts: a list screen joins detail tables or computes aggregate counts for every matching row
the UI only needs the current page plus a has-more signal
agents are tempted to preserve exact total counts while adding filters or hotfixes

trigger_signals.description: The query computes window counts, detail joins, or aggregates before LIMIT/OFFSET or cursor paging.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Move to a two-phase query: cheap candidate IDs first, expensive work only for the selected page.

trigger_signals.description: The UI demands an exact total even though the operation is primarily page navigation.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: Treat exactness as a product contract; use limit+1 has-more or labelled approximations if acceptable.

trigger_signals.description: EXPLAIN shows large intermediate rows for a screen that displays only a small page.
trigger_signals.agent_interpretation: The page boundary is in the wrong phase.

negative_signals.description: The product explicitly requires a globally exact total before showing any page.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: Then keep the exact count but budget it, cache it, or run it off the hot request path.

negative_signals.description: The filtered candidate set is already small and bounded before aggregates run.
negative_signals.why_it_matters: The additional two-phase machinery may not be necessary.

common_wrong_assumptions: A read-only list query is safe because it does not mutate data.
LIMIT at the end protects every earlier aggregate.
Exact total counts are harmless UI polish.

first_checks.check: Run EXPLAIN or ORM logging and identify whether candidate IDs are bounded before detail joins and aggregates.
first_checks.why: The expensive phase should operate on the page, not the whole match set.

first_checks.check: Prototype a limit+1 candidate-ID query and compare latency at realistic filter cardinality.
first_checks.why: Limit+1 proves has-more without a global count.

first_checks.check: Review UI copy for exact-total claims.
first_checks.why: Changing an exact number to approximate or has-more is a user-visible contract change, not a hidden performance patch.

decision_rules.condition: Expensive joins or aggregates run before the page boundary.
decision_rules.then: Filter and sort cheap candidate IDs, fetch limit+1, then join or aggregate only those IDs.

decision_rules.condition: The exact global count is not required for the user decision.
decision_rules.then: Expose has_more or an explicitly labelled approximation instead of a hot exact count.

decision_rules.condition: Exact totals are required and expensive.
decision_rules.then: Cache, precompute, or run the exact count in a separately budgeted path.

do_not: Do not run detail joins, window counts, or aggregates across an unbounded list because the final page is small.
Do not silently replace exact totals with approximate labels without changing the UI contract.
Do not treat this as the same trap as hot polling or cartesian join blow-up; cross-check those records separately.

Do not collapse this with hot-count-polling-can-become-the-incident or cartesian-distinct-counts-can-dos-a-production-db; this record is specifically about paging candidate IDs before detail aggregation.

agent_directives.preferred_next_step: Inspect the query phase order and move the page boundary before expensive aggregation when the screen only needs one page.

risk.notes: This record is de-identified agent guidance. It does not authorize bypassing maintainer, security, publication, production, billing, data, permission, or destructive-action gates.
